title: Ethiopian Lamb Key Wat
localName: የበግ ቀይ ወጥ — Ye-Beg Key Wat
community: All of Ethiopia — the celebration lamb version of the red stew
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Ye-Beg Key Wat — the celebration version of Key Wat using young lamb instead of beef. Served at Easter (Fasika), Ethiopian Christmas (Genna), and Timkat — the lamb version of the red stew carries even greater cultural weight than the beef version.
longDesc: Ye-Beg Key Wat is the pinnacle of Ethiopian celebration cooking — the lamb key wat served at the most important religious celebrations. The fat of young lamb in the berbere sauce produces an even richer, more fragrant result than beef key wat.
ingredients: 1 kg young lamb — bone-in, cut into portions
steps: Dry caramelise onions — 20 minutes, no oil.
Add berbere. Toast in kibbeh 3—4 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Add pierced eggs for the last 15 minutes.
chefTips: Young lamb becomes more tender than beef at the same cooking time.
The lamb fat enriches the berbere sauce — the result is more unctuous than beef key wat.
commonMistakes: Same as ETH021 — dry-caramelise the onions without fail.
cookingScience: Young lamb fat (predominantly oleic acid and short-chain fatty acids) has a lower melting point than beef fat — it renders out more rapidly into the sauce, producing a more richly unctuous result at the same cooking temperature.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian highland lamb — slaughtered specifically for the celebration.
healthBenefits: The eggs provide additional complete protein.
culturalNote: Ye-Beg Key Wat is the Easter morning dish of Ethiopian Orthodox Christians — prepared after the 55-day Lenten fast, the lamb slaughtered at dawn, the wat cooking through the morning as the family returns from the overnight Easter service. It is the most anticipated meal of the Ethiopian year.
